 Naji Marshall, Max Christie, Zaccharie Risacher, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 The Mavericks won’t have Cooper Flagg or Kyrie Irving on Saturday, with the former facing an extended absence after injuring his shoulder during Friday’s win over the Pacers. As a result, Marshall and Risacher will start, with Naji offering a higher ceiling for fantasy managers seeking a streamer. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is now probable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Dealing with a sore right hip, Risacher was initially questionable for Saturday’s game. With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) out and Kyrie Irving (knee) downgraded to doubtful, Risacher may have more offensive opportunities. However, Naji Marshall is a better option for managers seeking a streamer. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher had 11 points off the bench in Friday’s win over the Pacers. With the Mavericks’ lengthy injury report, he could play at least 30 minutes again, though he’s probably not worth streaming in most fantasy leagues. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher scored 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a steal, three blocks, and a three in 32 minutes against the Pacers. 
 He started the first half with 11 points and ended the game with 11 points. Risacher took advantage of all the easy opportunities in front of him. He got out in transition and took efficient shots. It seems like the Mavs are really prioritizing him and will get ample opportunities this season, even if it’s not a starter. Dusty May likes to play players with length, skill, and athleticism and Risacher can fit that. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) has been ruled out against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Martin will start the season on the injury report. However, Dallas has more than enough depth in the frontcourt to make up for his absence. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher may take on a few extra minutes. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Zaccharie Risacher has been traded to the Mavericks in a deal that sends Luguentz Dort and Ryan Nembhard to the Hawks and three second-round picks to the Thunder. 
 The former No. 1 overall pick wasn’t able to figure things out in Atlanta, but he’ll get a fresh start in Dallas. With Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz running the show for the Mavs, they have rebuilt this roster around Cooper Flagg by adding multiple new players in the frontcourt, including Risacher, Santi Aldama and Morez Johnson. Risacher’s role will likely be limited off the bench to start his tenure with Dallas, though a fresh start on a rebuilding team could yield him the opportunity to develop into the player the Hawks hoped he would become. The three second-round picks heading to OKC are Chicago’s 2027 pick from Dallas and most favorable picks in 2031 and 2032 from Atlanta. 
 Onyeka Okongwu 
 ATL 
 Forward-Center 
 #17 
 Onyeka Okongwu (finger) and Jonathan Kuminga (knee) are questionable for Sunday’s game against the Heat. 
 Okongwu and Kuminga sitting out Sunday’s regular-season finale would free up rotation minutes for multiple players. That includes Zaccharie Risacher, whose playing time has decreased with Kuminga in the fold, Asa Newell and Mouhamed Gueye. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher did not play in Wednesday’s loss to the Cavaliers. 
 After playing seven minutes in Monday’s loss to the Knicks, the first overall pick in the 2024 draft did not play at all on Wednesday. Jonathan Kuminga has seemingly absorbed the minutes that once went to Risacher. Logging 30 minutes, Kuminga finished with 24 points (11-of-20 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers. An afterthought in fantasy basketball since the All-Star break, it’s fair to wonder about Risacher’s future in Atlanta, especially if he racks up more DNP-CDs during the postseason. 
 Dyson Daniels 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dyson Daniels (toe) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 Daniels is officially out after being listed as questionable on the initial injury report. Zaccharie Risacher is the potential replacement in the starting lineup, giving the second-year a higher fantasy ceiling. 
 Dyson Daniels 
 ATL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dyson Daniels (toe) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 Daniels, who played 32 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Celtics, is dealing with a sprained left great toe. If he can’t play against the Kings, Zaccharie Risacher could move back into the starting lineup. While he has not been the most reliable fantasy option, Risacher could be worth streaming in deep leagues, given the matchup.

 Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 28 points (10-of-18 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist, four steals and four three-pointers in a 125-121 loss to the Cavaliers on Saturday.
 Even if the Nets are going to struggle again this season, Porter is certainly going to get his buckets. He’ll have a good chance to lead the Nets in scoring, even if Julius Randle is a threat to that title. He was a fantasy stud last season, but through two games, he has been even better by becoming a strong source of steals with seven so far this year. That pace won’t continue, but he may be able to hover around one per game like he did last season.

 Mikel Brown Jr. finished with eight points (3-of-10 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Cavaliers on Saturday.
 Brown hasn’t seen the volume of minutes that other rookies have because he is still recovering from an ankle injury, but he was able to showcase some flashes of why the Nets took him with the No. 7 overall pick. Head coach Jordi Fernandez said before the game that Brown will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back against the Pacers on Sunday. His next chance to suit up will be in Boston on Tuesday.

 Kyle Kuzma recorded 14 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds and three assists in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 After totaling 19 points, 15 rebounds and seven assists in Milwaukee’s first two games, Kuzma recorded a double-double on Saturday. While there weren’t any defensive stats to speak of, the percentages were good, and those rostering Kuzma will take the points and rebounds. The Bucks play three games during Week 2, starting with the rival Pacers on Monday night.

 Kel'el Ware

 Center

 Player Stats

 Kel’el Ware produced 19 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 The past two days reminded everyone why Ware is such a frustrating player to roster in fantasy basketball. After a subpar showing in the Bucks’ loss to the Bulls on Friday, the 7-footer rebounded and produced his best effort of the season’s first week. Ware recorded a complete stat line against the 76ers, including his first double-double of the season. Meanwhile, starting center Myles Turner went scoreless, contributing just five rebounds, one assist and one block in 20 minutes. As a result, the team benched him during the fourth quarter, with Ware picking up those minutes.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Jaquez has started his first season in Milwaukee strong, scoring at least 19 points in each of his first three games. Against the 76ers, he shot over 50 percent from the field and added solid rebound and assist numbers. Jaquez has yet to record a steal or blocked shot this season, but the rebounding and offensive output have been good. Set to hit restricted free agency in the summer, Jaquez is well positioned to deliver top-100 value in category leagues.

 Nate Ament accounted for one point (1-of-4 FTs), three rebounds and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Ament made his official NBA debut on Saturday, and unfortunately, it didn’t go well. The rookie missed his lone field-goal attempt and shot 1-of-4 from the foul line, while also picking up five fouls in 11 minutes. Even without LeBron James, Philadelphia isn’t a good matchup for Ament at this stage in his career. But it’s something to build on, and he’ll have plenty of chances to make good on his perceived upside throughout the season.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 VJ Edgecombe amassed 17 points (5-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 On a night when Joel Embiid recorded a triple-double, Edgecombe posted his eighth career double-double. The 76ers guard shot 5-of-10 from beyond the arc, a welcome development after going 1-of-7 from deep in wins over the Knicks and Cavaliers. Given Philadelphia’s offensive firepower, Edgecombe will get plenty of catch-and-shoot opportunities, even on nights when the rotation isn’t whole. Consistently taking advantage of those chances should raise his fantasy ceiling.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Tyrese Maxey recorded 26 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 Maxey finished the first and third quarters of Saturday’s win with buzzer-beaters, with one being a half-court shot. The 76ers’ point guard has scored at least 26 points in all three games this season, attempting 19 shots or more in each. Neither Maxey’s usage nor his production has suffered so far, and he’s especially well-positioned to feast in back-to-backs. LeBron James sat out Saturday’s game, and Joel Embiid won’t play on Sunday against the Pistons, which should be good news for those rostering Maxey.
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Recap

 Jaylen Brown accounted for 27 points (9-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 Brown did what he could to ensure that he’d celebrate a win on his 30th birthday, as he was one of three 76ers to score at least 26 points. According to NBC Sports Philadelphia, this is the first team JB has played on that has ranked in the top-10 in the league in pace. While it’s still extremely early, the returns have been positive for Brown and the 76ers. Philadelphia has one more Week 1 game, facing the Pistons on Sunday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Dean Wade finished Saturday’s win over the Bucks with seven points (2-of-3 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, three steals, one block and two three-pointers.
 After missing Philadelphia’s first two games with an ankle injury, Wade made his 76ers debut as a starter, stepping in for LeBron James (sciatica). The veteran forward produced solid value in steals, blocks and three-pointers, but more encouraging was Wade’s ability to play close to 30 minutes. The 76ers face Detroit on Sunday, and they may decide to sit Wade for injury management reasons. Consider him questionable for that one.
